name: Viking siege of Paris
summary: A Viking fleet of reportedly 700 ships and 30,000 warriors (likely exaggerated) besieges Paris (November 885 – October 886), attempting to sail past it to raid Burgundy. Count Odo of Paris and Bishop Gozlin organize a heroic 11-month defense of the two bridges across the Seine, preventing the Vikings from passing. King Charles the Fat arrives with a large army but pays tribute and allows the Vikings to pass through anyway, a humiliation that contributes to his deposition. Odo's defense makes him so popular he is elected King of West Francia (888).

_quarry.structural_significance: Demonstrates the failure of Carolingian monarchy to defend its people; Odo's defense creates the Capetian family's prestige; the siege is a pivotal moment in the transition from Carolingian to Capetian France
